chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who perfumes herself, then goes out from her house, is cursed until she returns to her house, whenever she returns.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman wearing perfume when going out in public according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the etiquette of *khusuf* (modesty) in public spaces. The 'curse' mentioned is understood by Shia scholars as a spiritual consequence for exposing one's adornment (*zeenah*) to non-mahram men, reinforcing the Quranic injunction for women to draw their veils over themselves.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whichever woman perfumes herself, then goes out from her house, so she is cursed until she return to her house whenever she returns’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
If a woman wears perfumes then goes out of her house, she is then cursed and condemned until she returns to her home whenever she does.’”
